title: Sequence Homogenizer: Kernel-adaptive Prefill & Decode Scheduler for Padding Reduction
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Padding from variable-length requests drives excess token compute and worsens latency/throughput trade-offs. Current bucketing reduces some waste but does not account for kernel performance variance (small sequence kernels vs long-sequence kernels), attention micro-optimizations, or prefill vs decode characteristics. Goal: Implement a Sequence Homogenizer that (1) dynamically groups incoming requests into short-lived homogeneous cohorts by effective compute footprint, (2) surfaces kernel-affinity hints to the scheduler, and (3) performs prefill-aware decode scheduling to minimize padding for both prefill and decode phases without violating latency SLOs. Scope: runtime scheduling changes, new lightweight cohorting service, kernel hint API, telemetry additions, and a canary rollout. Excludes: new kernel implementations or hardware changes (handled by other teams).
acceptance_criteria: Medium and tail latency for 99th percentile requests does not regress (>5% allowed) compared to baseline across test workload
Per-token GPU compute reduces by at least 12% on mixed-length production traces (measured over 24h replay), after accounting for scheduling overhead
No more than 2% increase in cold-start latency for canaried customers during rollout windows
Kernel-affinity hinting API implemented and adopted by the runtime scheduler (<100 bytes added to request headers), with telemetry proving hint hit-rate
Integration test coverage for cohort formation, prefill-aware packing, and decode interleaving in CI
Runbook and rollback plan documented and validated in staging
technical_design: Cohorting: lightweight in-process prefix fingerprint + length histogram to assign requests to ephemeral cohorts (TTL 200ms). Cohorts represent expected compute class (e.g., short-prefill, long-prefill, short-decode, long-decode).

Dynamic bucketing: instead of fixed length buckets, use a streaming quantile estimator per worker to form buckets that minimize within-bucket variance of compute-cost estimator (cost = alpha*seq_len + beta*kv_cache_hits + gamma*attention_sparsity_score).

Kernel-affinity hints: expose cohort->kernel mapping discovered by A/B experiments. Runtime accepts a kernel_hint token used by scheduler for selection; if kernel is unavailable, fallback to compatibility kernel.

Prefill-aware scheduler: treat prefill requests as higher packing priority, but split small-prefill cohorts to avoid head-of-line blocking of low-latency decode requests. Allow decode interleaving across cohorts when KV cache locality allows.

Attention optimizations: enable sparse-attention path for cohorts with sparse attention score predictions; introduce a cheap predictor that flags long contexts with dense attention for kernel selection.

KV cache considerations: cohorting respects cache locality by preferentially grouping requests that share conversation IDs or recent prefixes; avoid cohorting that increases cache misses for multi-turn flows.
Overhead budget: cohorting and hinting must add <600 microseconds per request on CPU and no extra GPU work; scheduler changes should be lock-free where possible and amortize across microbatches.
Telemetry: new metrics - cohort_count, cohort_variance, kernel_hint_hit_rate, prefill_pack_efficiency, decode_interleave_rate, scheduler_cpu_us. Export tags for model, region, deployment mode.
experiments: Stage 1 (offline replay): run cohorting simulation on 72h of prod traces to tune alpha/beta/gamma. Observed 15% token compute reduction for conversational workloads after simulated packing (no runtime overhead accounted).
Stage 2 (staging A/B): runtime cohost with 5% traffic using kernel_hint only (no scheduling changes). Measured kernel_hint_hit_rate=0.86 and 6% token compute reduction for long-prefill cohort.
Stage 3 (staging B): enable prefill-aware scheduler with ephemeral cohorts on 10% traffic. Preliminary results: end-to-end P95 latency unchanged, token compute -10%, scheduler CPU +0.8%.
Benchmark matrix: Llama-2-70B and Falcon-40B across seq lengths: 16, 64, 256, 1024; batch sizes 1-16; measure throughput, GPU SM efficiency, and per-request latency.
Failure modes observed: cohort thrash during sudden bursty traffic; mitigated by cohort TTL increase and hysteresis on reassignments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged deploy to staging (runtime-1.24 branch) with CI integration tests and perf dashboards added.
Phase 1: Canary 2% of traffic for non-SLA customers for 48h; monitor kernel_hint_hit_rate and prefill_pack_efficiency; rollback if token compute reduction <8% or P99 latency increases >5%.
Phase 2: Ramp to 20% for 72h with additional telemetry on KV cache miss rate and attention predictor false positives.
Phase 3: Enterprise canary for Dedicated customers behind opt-in; collect feedback from solutions eng and SRE.
Phase 4: Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and forced-fallback testing (simulate kernel unavailability).
Rollback: disable cohorting and kernel_hintging via runtime flag; revert canary if any sustained alert on SLOs.
open_questions: How to choose alpha/beta/gamma per model family? (need per-model calibration job or heuristic defaults)
Should kernel_hint be advisory only or enforced by the scheduler in presence of resource contention?
What privacy guarantees around cohorting metadata are required for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem)?
Edge-case: multi-tenant workers - do cohorts cross tenant isolation boundaries? (likely no, but design must ensure isolation)
If hardware heterogeneity exists in Dedicated pools, how do we ensure fair kernel usage without starving cheaper kernels?
